notes: Both figures come from LG's own US press-release PDFs still hosted live on lg.com (no web.archive.org snapshot needed for this entry, unlike most other dead LG pages). The 169.5 x 74.5 x 10.9 mm figure is the device in Basic Mode, i.e. with the main screen swivelled shut over the second screen - recorded as 'closed'. LG publishes NO dimensions for Swivel Mode (the T-shaped open state), so 'open' is entirely null. Both displays are recorded because both are physical panels present at all times: the 6.8" main screen that swivels, and the 3.9" second screen beneath it, which is only exposed in Swivel Mode. LG writes the second screen's panel as 'G-OLED' in the spec list; recorded as OLED per the SPEC enum. Refresh rates are not published by LG for either panel - null. hinge.max_angle_deg 90 is LG's own '90 degrees', stated as a clockwise rotation of the entire front of the phone; hinge.axis is null because a swivel rotates about an axis perpendicular to the display plane, which neither 'long' nor 'short' describes. LG states durability as '200,000 swivels', a Hydraulic Damper in the hinge, a dual lock mechanism, and 'Thermoplastic polyoxymethylene is applied to the back of the Main Screen' - that last is an internal surface treatment, not a frame/back/cover-glass spec, so materials remain null. LG describes the body only as 'slim but tough composite materials'. Battery 4,000 mAh; Snapdragon 765G; colors Aurora Gray / Illusion Sky. Released date is US/Verizon first availability; LG notes 'AT&T and T-Mobile will offer it later this fall'.
